sun.upright:
Mars rules Aries, and the Ten of Cups is Mars in Pisces, so what you've drawn is your own ruler turning up in softer clothes. Pisces sits right behind your sign, the twelfth next to the first, and neighbouring signs like that have very little in common. An Aries Sun wants to get there first and under its own steam. This card takes that same drive and asks what it's for, and the answer it gives is a houseful of people who are pleased to see you walk in.

That's an odd thing to hear when your pride is built on doing it yourself. From the inside it can feel like being asked to stand still. Water on fire makes steam, and you'll know the feeling, the restless evening where everything's fine and you can't settle, where you go looking for a job to do or an argument to have because contentment doesn't feel like getting anywhere. I see this a lot with Aries Suns. You'd fight for your family in a second. Sitting with them when there's nothing to fight for is harder, and that's exactly where the card is pointing.

At work it might be the promotion you're chasing that would take you away from the people you'd actually name if someone asked what it was all for. With a partner it's being brilliant in a crisis and oddly absent on a quiet Sunday. With kids, or nieces and nephews, or a younger brother, it's being the fun one who turns up with a plan and leaves before the washing up. Pick one ordinary evening and stay for all of it, start to finish, without organising anything.
sun.reversed:
With your own ruler upside down in Pisces, the drive tends to go one of two ways. Either it fights for the idea of a happy family and gets impatient with the actual one, the partner who won't cheer on cue, the kids who won't sit still for the photo. Or it turns away from home altogether, because home doesn't give an Aries Sun anything to win, and you pour everything into work, sport, the next project, and call it providing.

Either way the people at home get the tired version of you. It shows in the argument about who does more around the house, which is usually about something else, and in the birthday you nearly missed. Ask the person closest to you what they'd like more of from you. Whatever they say, don't argue with it, even in your head, for a full day.

moon.upright:
Anger comes fast with an Aries Moon, and so does forgiveness, often inside ten minutes. Mars rules your Moon's sign. When the Ten of Cups turns up here it's that same planet sitting in Pisces, the softest water in the zodiac, and the effect is a bit like a hot pan put in the sink. There's a hiss. Feelings that would usually come out as a snap are coming out as tenderness, or tears, or a sudden fierce protectiveness about somebody you love.

That can be unsettling. Your Moon calms down by doing something, and water and fire are opposed elements, so the card is asking you to calm down by staying put and being looked after, which for you can feel close to losing. You'll notice the temper is shorter when you're tired or hungry, and that a lot of what looks like irritation is really worry. Somebody at home is on your mind, and you'd sooner fight their battles than admit how much it's getting to you. Being the protector feels safe. Letting someone protect you back is a lot harder, to be honest.

With a partner, it's the sharp reply that really means 'I was scared when you didn't text'. With a parent it's being furious on their behalf, at a landlord or a sibling who let them down. In your body it's a restless charge that won't burn off. Go for a hard walk or a swim before the difficult conversation, then have it sitting down, with the kettle on.
moon.reversed:
Upside down, this is steam with the lid on. The anger an Aries Moon would normally let out and be done with gets swallowed for the sake of peace at home, because Pisces wants everyone getting along. But Mars is your Moon's own ruler, and it doesn't go quietly. It leaks. Slammed cupboards, a clipped tone, a sulk you'd deny was a sulk. Or it builds and builds and comes out over something tiny, and then you feel dreadful and overdo the kindness to make up for it.

The family usually feels it before you name it. Kids go quiet around you, and a partner starts checking your face when they walk in. Sleep gets hot and short. The fix is dull and it works. Say the small annoyance while it's small, on the day it happens, in one sentence, and then let it go the way your Moon already knows how to.

rising.upright:
Aries rising walks in first and asks questions later. People read you as quick, direct, maybe a bit much before they've had a coffee. Mars is your chart ruler, and with the Ten of Cups drawn for the mask, the ruler of your whole chart is sitting in Pisces, soft and open-handed. So people are meeting a warmer version of you. The edge is still there, it's just pointed outward on behalf of a group. You come across as someone with a crew, a family, people you'd go to the wall for.

Your usual way of starting is to go alone and fast. This card starts things by gathering people. That's a real adjustment, and Pisces and Aries being next-door signs doesn't help, since they share almost nothing. From an Aries Ascendant, Pisces is also the twelfth house, the hidden end of the chart, so a lot of this warmth is coming from somewhere you don't usually show strangers. You may catch yourself being gentle with someone in the first five minutes and wonder where that came from.

In a new job it looks like being the one who organises the team lunch in week two, and people remembering that long after they've forgotten your sales figures. On a first date it's giving off something steady and homely that you didn't quite intend, and the other person relaxing because of it. With new neighbours it's being the one who notices the old man next door hasn't put his bins out. When you're next walking into a room of strangers, find out who they belong to before you tell them what you do.
rising.reversed:
Coming across as defensive is the risk here. With Mars ruling your chart and the card reversed, the protectiveness shows before the warmth does, and new people can feel like they've wandered onto somebody's property. You bristle when a stranger says something about your family, your team, your town. Or it tips the other way and you arrive performing an easy, happy life you're not really living, all smiles and good news, because the first impression matters so much to an Aries Ascendant.

At work that looks like the new colleague who asked an innocent question about your department and got a lecture. At the school gate or the club it's a brightness people can tell is effortful. Walk into the next new place with nothing to defend. Let someone else set the tone for the first ten minutes and see what they do with it.

sun.upright:
You've probably looked at the little house in the Ten of Cups and priced the renovation before noticing the rainbow over it. Taurus Suns want something solid of their own, made properly, and they want to be known as the one who made it. This card is home and family, the thing a lot of Taureans are quietly building toward all their lives, and it sits well with you. Pisces and Taurus are sextile, two signs apart, an easy opening. Water and earth get on too. Whatever gets planted here takes its time and holds.

The snag is Mars. It's in detriment in Taurus, which means the card's planet is working against the grain of your sign, and you'll feel that as a reluctance to push. You'd happily spend ten years building a home with your hands. Picking a fight inside it, even a necessary one, is much harder, because it disturbs the peace you've worked for. So the effort goes into what you can make and fix and pay for, and the harder effort, the talk about who does what, the thing your partner said at Christmas, sits there getting heavier. Taurus is fixed. It can carry that weight a long time before anyone knows.

With money this is providing well and feeling a bit taken for granted. In your relationship it's showing love through a good meal and a warm house and not much talk. With your own parents it might be the family traditions you're keeping going single-handed. Some of what you've built is finished and deserves to be enjoyed. Take one Saturday off from improving anything and just use the place.
sun.reversed:
Mars in detriment gets stuck easily, and with the card reversed a Taurus Sun can dig in around home and call it loyalty. The house has to be kept a certain way. Sunday lunch has to be at yours. Your own plans for yourself get pushed back another year. Change of any kind feels like a threat to everything you've built, so the people inside it start working around you instead of with you.

Money is usually where it surfaces first, the purchase you won't agree to, or the one you make to cheer yourself up after a bad week. A partner might have raised something months ago that you've been too comfortable to answer. Take one fixed habit at home, something you've always insisted on, and ask the others whether it still works for them. Listen to the answer with your hands still.

moon.upright:
Comfort is physical for a Taurus Moon. A full fridge, clean sheets, the same chair, someone whose smell you know. This is the sort of card this Moon relaxes into, because it's a picture of a home that has been worked at and now simply holds. Pisces is sextile to Taurus and the two elements are friends, water softening earth, earth giving water somewhere to sit. You may find the ordinary pleasures are doing a lot for you, and that you need them more than you'd say.

The awkward part is what the card's planet does here. Mars is in detriment in Taurus, so anger has a hard time moving in you. It sinks. You don't flare up, you go heavy and slow and very polite, and the resentment gets stored somewhere around the stomach. The card's gentleness makes that worse in a way, because it's so tempting to keep things nice. Family can go months without knowing you were hurt, and when it finally comes out it's older and bigger than it needed to be.

Food is usually where it shows first, eating for comfort, or losing your appetite without noticing. Sleep can go long and heavy. With a partner it's the lovely evening in that steps around the conversation you both know is there. With a parent it's the visit where you help in the garden and say nothing about what's actually bothering you. Next time something stings, say so within a day, calmly, while it's still small enough to hand over.
moon.reversed:
For a Taurus Moon, the reversed card is comfort turned into a hiding place. Home becomes somewhere to shut the door on hard feelings, and the soothing habits, the second glass, the takeaway, the series watched back to back, start doing a job they were never meant to do. Mars in detriment here can't bring itself to push, so nothing gets raised, and the household settles into a very pleasant stalemate.

Your body will usually tell you first, a heaviness, a sore neck, sleep that doesn't refresh. Money leaks a little on small treats. The people you live with sense something's off and can't find the edge of it. Pick the one thing you haven't said at home, and say it at the kitchen table, in daylight, over something to eat.

rising.upright:
Calm is the first thing people notice about Taurus rising. They see someone unhurried and pleasant, probably a good cook, and they tend to trust you before you've said much. The Ten of Cups on that doorway makes you look like the settled one in any room, someone with a home to go back to and people who'd notice if you were late. Pisces sits sextile to your rising sign and the elements get along, so the card suits how you come across. Count round from Taurus and Pisces lands in your eleventh house, among friends and groups, so you may find new people treating you like family quite quickly.

Mars is the difficulty. It's in detriment in Taurus, so your starts are slow and you hardly ever chase. The card wants you to reach out, to invite, to gather people, and a Taurus Ascendant would sooner wait to be asked and then turn up with a cake. That works most of the time. It also means you can go a whole year being liked by a new group and never quite being in it, because you left it to them to make the first move.

At a new job that's being thought of as lovely and steady and left off the drinks list by accident. In dating it's giving off 'long-term' so clearly that anyone after something casual walks straight past, which is probably fine by you. With neighbours it's the wave and the smile and the dinner invitation you keep meaning to make. So make it, and name a date when you do.
rising.reversed:
People might be reading you as closed off. The easy calm of a Taurus Ascendant, with the card upside down, can look like a door that's already shut, a person with their family and friends sorted who doesn't need anyone new. Mars in detriment makes it worse, since you won't push past that impression yourself. Or you're showing strangers a very tidy picture of your life and keeping the mess well out of view.

Invitations can dry up without you quite noticing why, and a new workplace stays friendly and never gets personal. Online it can be the lovely photos of the garden and the dinner table that get likes and no real conversations. Tell one new person something ordinary and slightly messy about your life, the burnt dinner, the broken fence, and see how quickly they warm up.

sun.upright:
Settling down has never been top of a Gemini Sun's list. You want to be interesting and interested, and to keep enough doors open that life never gets dull. Of all the cups, the tenth is the one where every door leads back to the same house. Pisces squares Gemini. Both are mutable, three signs apart, and a square is friction that forces a decision, which is roughly what this card is asking of you. Mars, meanwhile, holds no rank in Gemini and picks up the manners of Mercury, your ruler, so the card's drive is coming through words, messages, plans and talking things through.

From the inside it's a split. Part of you wants to belong completely, to have your people and your place, and part of you panics slightly the moment that looks settled, because being known that well might mean being pinned down. Mars also rules the middle ten degrees of Gemini, the decan of the Nine of Swords, the card of lying awake at three in the morning. If you're wondering why the happiness comes with an undertow of worry, that link is part of it. You can be in the middle of a lovely family day and running through everything that could go wrong with it.

With siblings this often shows as a reconnection, the long phone call, the group chat coming back to life. With a partner it's the conversation about the future that you keep turning into a joke. At work it's a team you're fonder of than you'd admit. Let one thing stay settled without testing it. You don't need to explain it or keep an exit plan.
sun.reversed:
When the card turns over for a Gemini Sun, belonging starts to feel like a trap and you talk your way out of it. Mars working through Mercury gets quick and cutting. The joke at the family dinner that lands a bit too hard, the clever reason you can't come this year, the reply that wins the argument and loses the person. Or you keep five circles of friends at arm's length so no single one of them gets the whole of you.

Siblings are often where it shows, an old rivalry picked back up over something small. In a relationship it's being charming about everything except commitment. At work it's being everybody's friend and nobody's colleague. Choose one group you actually care about and turn up for the boring part, the clean-up after the party or the admin nobody wants, without making a joke about it.

moon.upright:
Talking is how a Gemini Moon calms down. Say the feeling, get a reply, feel better. The Ten of Cups brings a kind of fullness that doesn't need discussing, and water and air have to be introduced to each other, they don't mix on their own. You're likely to notice feelings that are bigger and slower than the ones you usually get, affection for your family, a sudden soft spot for an old friend, and your first impulse will be to describe them to somebody.

Pisces squares your Moon's sign, both of them mutable, and that friction is part of why it feels restless. Mars is only a guest in Gemini, borrowing Mercury's habits, so strong feeling tends to come out of you as argument, or as a flood of messages sent all at once. Then there's the Nine of Swords. Mars rules that middle stretch of Gemini too, and it can mean the happier you feel, the more your mind lists what could go wrong. You love them, so you worry. That's normal, and it can keep you up.

Sleep is usually where it shows. A busy head at night, the phone checked once more. With a sibling or a cousin it's a long catch-up that leaves you oddly moved. With a partner it's wanting reassurance and asking for it sideways, through questions about plans. When the feeling is good, how long can you sit in the room with it before you reach for your phone?
moon.reversed:
Reversed, the Gemini Moon's way with words turns against the feeling. You can talk about your family for an hour and never once say you miss them. Mars going through Mercury sharpens everything, so the family group chat gets tense, a message gets read the wrong way, and you're drafting replies at midnight you'd never say to anyone's face. The Nine of Swords side of Mars in Gemini gets louder as well, the worry looping over people you can't do anything for.

It shows in sleep, in a jittery stomach, and in picking at a partner over small things because the big thing hasn't been said. A sibling may well be involved. Put the phone in another room for one evening and ring the person instead. If you can, go round and see them.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising arrives chatting. Quick, funny, curious, and hard to place, because you seem to know a bit about everybody. The Ten of Cups on your mask adds something people don't expect from you, a warm, settled look, like someone with a close family or a tight crew behind them. From a Gemini Ascendant, Pisces is the tenth sign along, your tenth house, the top of the chart, so this card's sign sits right in your public life. You may find you're seen as the one who holds a group together, at work especially.

The square between Pisces and Gemini is where it rubs. Both are mutable, both change shape, and they want different things. Your rising sign starts things by talking. The card starts things by belonging. With Mars a guest in Gemini and taking Mercury's lead, you tend to rush the warmth, calling someone a mate in week one, promising a catch-up you haven't got room for. It comes from a good place. It can also leave people unsure whether you meant it.

In a new team this shows as becoming the social glue very fast, the birthday card, the group chat, the Friday drinks. In dating it's coming across as ready for something serious, which may surprise you and may also please you. With neighbours or a new club it's the introductions you make between people who go on to become good friends. Follow up one of those introductions properly, with a day and a time.
rising.reversed:
Upside down on a Gemini Ascendant, the card makes the warmth read as patter. You're friendly with everyone and people can't tell where they stand, and Mars borrowing Mercury's quickness can make a first meeting feel like a performance of closeness. Or you swing the other way and keep it so light that nobody gets anywhere near you, all jokes and questions and no answers.

In a new job that's the colleague everybody likes and nobody confides in. In a friendship it's 'we must catch up' said five times with no catch-up. At family gatherings it's working the room and going home without one real conversation. Slow the next introduction down. Ask one question and stay with the answer for as long as the other person wants to talk.

sun.upright:
This card is close to a picture of what a Cancer Sun is trying to build. The couple with their arms round each other, the kids playing, the house behind them. Cancer is ruled by the Moon and wants to protect people and be the heart of a family, whatever shape the family takes. Pisces is trine to Cancer, both water signs, so the card speaks your sign's own language. That amplifies things, for better and sometimes for too much. You'll feel very sure of what matters to you.

The complication is Mars. It's in fall in Cancer, uncomfortable in your sign, and it has to find an indirect way to do its job. So you'll fight hard for the people you love and barely manage to ask for one thing for yourself. Pride for a Cancer Sun is usually about being needed. The card's warmth lands right on that, and it can make it harder to notice you've been the one holding everything for a long while, that you're tired, and that you'd quite like someone to hold you for a change. Cancer is cardinal, a starting sign, but it starts things sideways, by looking after someone else first.

With your mum, or whoever raised you, there may be a softening, an old tension letting up. In your own household it's being the one who remembers everything, the dentist, the birthdays, the lunchboxes. At work it's being the unofficial parent of the team. Ask for one thing that's only for you. Ask directly, in words, and let somebody else sort it out.
sun.reversed:
Mars in fall does sly things when the card is reversed. A Cancer Sun may be keeping the family together through sheer effort and resenting every minute of it, or managing everyone's feelings so nobody has to see yours. The ideal of a close, happy home starts running the show. You host the Christmas nobody else wants to host, because it matters to you that it looks right, and your own plans get pushed to next year again.

It comes out in small martyrdoms. The extra load of washing done with a sigh, the favour that comes with a reminder later. A partner or grown-up kids may feel vaguely guilty around you without knowing why. Hand one family job over to someone else this time, and don't check how they did it afterwards.

moon.upright:
A Cancer Moon lives on belonging. You need to know your people are safe and that there's a place where you can put your guard down. The card is water in a water sign, trine to your Moon, so the card is saying something you'd understand without being told. When this comes up for your tides you're probably feeling very full, grateful for someone, homesick for someone else, moved by small family things other people would walk straight past.

With that much water it's easy to go under a little. Mars is in fall in Cancer, uncomfortable and unheard, and that affects what you do with the harder feelings. Anger doesn't have a straight path out of you. It turns into hurt, or into a mood that fills the kitchen, or into a memory from twenty years ago that arrives fully formed. You may feel like you're carrying the whole family's weather, and some of the time you are, because Cancer Moons tend to be the ones who notice.

Your mother, or whoever did the mothering, is likely to be on your mind in some way. The house itself matters too, and you might feel an urge to cook for people, fill the table, get everyone round. Your stomach will tell you before your head does when something's wrong. Have people over, by all means. If something's bothering you underneath, tell one of them, quietly, while you're doing the dishes together.
moon.reversed:
This is the Cancer Moon hurt and holding on to it. With Mars in fall and the card reversed, the anger has nowhere to go at all, so it goes into the past. Old family grievances come back as if they were yesterday, and you find yourself comparing the real family to the one you hoped you'd have. The shell goes up. People who love you are shut out, and part of you is waiting for them to knock.

It tends to show in eating and sleeping, too much or too little, and in the house going quiet in a way everyone can feel. A sibling or a parent may be at the centre of it. Write down the actual thing that hurt, in one line, without the history. Then decide whether to give it to the person or put it in the bin.

rising.upright:
Strangers tend to take Cancer rising for kind and a little reserved, probably somebody's favourite aunt or uncle, watching the room from behind a pleasant shell. Drawn for your mask, this card brings all of that forward. People see a family person, somebody warm who'll remember their kid's name, and they relax around you faster than usual. Pisces is trine to Cancer, water with water, and the card's softness sits easily on you. You look like someone with a home worth going back to, and people would like to be invited.

Mars is the awkward guest. It's in fall in Cancer, which makes your way of starting things indirect at the best of times. You'll look after people before you introduce yourself, and offer tea before you offer an opinion. Your sign's own card is The Chariot, and Cancer's way forward usually involves armour. This card asks you to go forward without it, arms up like the couple under the rainbow, and that feels exposed.

In a new job this is being quietly adopted as the one who looks after everybody, which is lovely and also a lot. In dating it's coming across as someone who wants the whole thing, the home, the kids, the Sunday roast, whether or not you'd planned to say so. With a new group of friends it's the first dinner you host. The first move is the hard part for you. Make it anyway, and make it an invitation, since inviting people is what you're good at.
rising.reversed:
First impressions can go a bit wrong for Cancer rising here. The warmth comes out as mothering, and new people feel managed before they feel welcome. Mars in fall makes you come at things sideways, so a stranger gets the hint and the look and never the straight request. Or the shell stays shut and you're polite and unreadable, and people assume you're cold when you're really just shy.

At a new workplace it means looking after everyone and being taken for granted by week three. In dating it's giving so much so early that the other person backs off. At the school gate or a new club it's hanging back at the edge of the group. Pick one new person and say plainly what you'd like from the connection, even if it's only a coffee.

sun.upright:
Nobody in the Ten of Cups gets to be the star. Have a look. The couple have their backs half to you, the kids are off playing, and everyone's attention is going up to the rainbow. For a Leo Sun that's an unusual kind of happiness to be handed, one where you aren't the centre of it. The Sun rules your sign, and Mars comes into Leo as a guest with no dignity of its own, lit by the Sun, so the card's drive comes out of you as generosity. Hosting, giving, making the day for everyone.

Pisces and Leo are quincunx, though, five signs apart with nothing in common, and the elements are at odds too, fire and water, steam or one putting the other out. You'll feel it at the big family occasion you organised, when everyone's having a lovely time and nobody's quite said thank you, and there's a small hurt you'd be embarrassed to name. Mars also rules the final stretch of Leo, twenty degrees onward, which is the Seven of Wands decan, the card of holding your ground. If your Sun is late in Leo you'll know the urge to defend your place in the family, your role, your recipe, your seat at the head of the table.

With your kids, or anyone younger you're close to, it can mean letting them shine at something you're good at. In love it's being the generous one and wanting that noticed. At work it's the team win you could claim and could also share. Some of the best days this card points to are ones where you're simply one of the family. Host something and let someone else make the toast.
sun.reversed:
Reversed for a Leo Sun, the card can turn family life into a stage. The birthday has to be perfect, the photos have to be good, and everyone has to be seen to be happy, because the picture reflects on you. Mars as the Sun's guest gets proud and a bit bossy about it. The Seven of Wands side comes out too, defending your place at the head of the table against anyone who'd like a turn.

Big occasions are where it shows, the wedding speech, the holiday, the party where you ran everything and enjoyed none of it. A partner may feel like a supporting act. Grown kids may quietly stop coming to the things you organise. Ask someone else to plan the next gathering, and go as a guest, with a bottle and no opinions.

moon.upright:
Warmth is what feeds a Leo Moon. Being adored, being chosen, knowing you matter to someone and hearing them say so. This card is love all around you, and on this Moon it tends to show up as feeling cherished, or wanting to be, very much. Mars is only a guest in Leo, lit by the Sun, so affection comes out of you in big gestures, the surprise, the present, the dinner for twelve.

The rub is the quincunx. Pisces and Leo have nothing in common, and fire and water either make steam or put each other out. Pisces love is quiet and spread thin, it goes to everyone. Your Moon wants to be loved in particular, and first. So you can be surrounded by a happy, affectionate family and still feel a small cold spot because nobody asked about your day. That's not vanity, or not only. A Leo Moon feels safe when it's seen, and a crowd can make it hard to be seen.

In a relationship this can be the nagging sense that you give more than you get, and the pride that stops you saying it. With friends it's being the life of the gathering and going home feeling a bit invisible. With kids, it can be a strong wish for them to be proud of you. The body carries it as a kind of heat, restless sleep, a flushed face after a party. Next time you need to be noticed, say so, lightly, to the person you want it from.
moon.reversed:
When this turns over on a Leo Moon, hurt pride starts running the household. Being overlooked at a family thing becomes a grudge that lasts for months, because Leo is fixed and holds on. Or you over-give to win the love back, the generous gesture that's really a question, and sulk when it isn't answered the way you wanted. The warmth your Moon lives on has been rationed, and you've started rationing yours back.

It comes up at gatherings, in the comparison with a sibling who seems to be the favourite, and with the partner who can't do anything right for a while. Sleep can go shallow. Say the plain thing to the person you're hurt by, in a sentence, without the performance around it, and let them answer before you decide how it went.

rising.upright:
Leo rising makes an entrance whether it means to or not. Good hair, a big smile, and the sense that the party has just started. The Ten of Cups on that doorway turns the warmth outward. People meet you as someone generous and loyal, with a family or a gang behind them, and they want to be part of it. The card's planet is a guest in Leo with no dignity there, lit by the Sun, your chart ruler, so the drive behind your first impression is warm and very visible.

The trouble is that this card doesn't do spotlights, and your Ascendant rather does. Pisces is quincunx to Leo, a constant small adjustment, and fire and water are opposites. You might find yourself toning it down to fit in with a group, and feeling a bit less like yourself for it. Or you go the other way and play host so fully that no one sees how much you'd like to be looked after. Mars also has a stake in the end of Leo, twenty to twenty-nine degrees, the Seven of Wands decan, and if your Ascendant falls there you'll recognise that slightly defensive first move, the need to establish your place early.

At work this is being the one who organises the leaving do, and doing it beautifully. On a date you come across as warm and serious, the kind of person someone could take home to meet their mum. At a new school gate or a new club it's being the welcoming one for everybody else. Let someone welcome you, the next time. Sit down at their table and accept whatever they're offering.
rising.reversed:
Reversed on a Leo Ascendant, the warmth can look staged. New people pick up a brightness that's a bit too bright, a family life described as perfect, a group you're clearly running. Mars as the Sun's guest pushes to be in charge of the fun, and that can come across as needing to be. Or the fire goes out altogether and you're flat and polite, waiting for someone to spark you up.

First meetings are where it shows, when you talk about your people so much the other person never gets a word in. At work it's the new colleague who feels you've already decided who's in the inner circle. Try going into the next new room as the quiet one. Ask about their people, and don't mention yours until someone asks.

sun.upright:
Picture the family barbecue a Virgo Sun has organised. The salads are labelled, there's a vegetarian option, somebody's allergy has been thought of, and you're at the edge of it all with a tea towel. You want to be useful and to do the job properly, and you'd like, just occasionally, for someone to notice. The Ten of Cups comes from Pisces, your opposite sign, the same axis seen from the other end. Virgo checks every detail. Pisces sees the whole and lets the details blur. The card is a picture of the whole day going well with nobody auditing it.

Mars has no special dignity in Virgo and takes its tone from Mercury, your ruler, so the card's drive shows up in you as effort and organisation. The lists, the rosters, the reminder texts, the meals planned in advance. That's real love, and the people around you run on it. The tension is that you make everyone else's happiness possible and then stand outside it checking whether it's good enough. Earth and water are friendly elements, so there's no real fight here, only an old habit of not letting yourself in. I've heard a lot of Virgo Suns describe a lovely family day entirely in terms of what went wrong.

At work this might be a team that's finally running smoothly because of something you set up. With your health it's routines quietly paying off. When your partner thanks you, you wave it away. Next time someone thanks you, say thanks back and leave it there. Don't explain what you'd have done differently.
sun.reversed:
Upside down for a Virgo Sun, the card can turn helping into criticism. You've done so much for the family that you've started keeping score, and it comes out as correction, the way someone stacks the dishwasher, the way the kids were dressed for the photo. Pisces on the other end of your axis wants things loose and forgiven, and reversed, you swing hard toward the Virgo end of it.

At home it looks like a partner who has stopped helping because it's never right, and at work like the team that leaves everything to you and then gets told off for it. Your body carries it too, in the gut or the jaw. For one whole weekend, let a household job be done badly by somebody else and don't comment on it.

moon.upright:
Tidy kitchen, bills paid, everyone accounted for. That's when a Virgo Moon can breathe. It feels safe by being useful. The Ten of Cups drawn here comes from Pisces, your Moon's opposite sign, and it asks for something harder, which is to feel safe while things are a bit of a mess, because the love is there anyway. Water and earth are friendly elements, so it isn't a hostile card for you. It's more like a hand on your shoulder telling you to sit down.

That's uncomfortable, if I'm honest. Mars is a visitor in Virgo, borrowing Mercury's habits, and so any strong feeling turns into a task. You're worried about your dad, so you research everything about his new tablets. You're hurt by a friend, so you reorganise the linen cupboard. Pisces at the other end of the axis would just feel it, cry maybe, be held. You don't have to stop being practical. Just notice the feeling under the practical bit, and let someone see it.

Your stomach is usually the first place this shows. Sleep too, when the list keeps running at night. With a partner, it's caring for them in a hundred ways and not quite asking to be cared for. With family it's being the organised one at the reunion and missing half the conversation. Let yourself be looked after once, in some small way, a meal made for you or a job done without your help. Notice what that feels like.
moon.reversed:
This one reversed makes a Virgo Moon anxious about the people it loves. Worry turns into checking, the texts, the calls, the hovering, and caring for everyone becomes a way of not feeling anything yourself. Mars, a visitor in your Moon's sign, gets picky under pressure, so small things at home start to grate out of all proportion. You may catch yourself tidying someone else's house.

Sleep usually suffers, and digestion, and your patience with a partner who never seems to notice what needs doing. A parent might be taking up a lot of your worry. Pisces, at the far end of your axis, would let a few of those things go. Write down, in one list, everything you're worrying about for other people. Then cross off anything you can't actually change, and put the list away.

rising.upright:
Pisces sits opposite Virgo, so with Virgo rising it's on your Descendant, the cusp of the seventh house, where partners and the people across the table live. So this card is being drawn from your partnership angle. People already take you for neat, capable and a bit reserved, the one who'll know where the first-aid kit is. What they're meeting in you with this card is somebody plainly ready to share a life, and the people drawn to you may bring the Pisces half, the softness and the mess and the big feelings.

Mars has no rank in Virgo and takes on Mercury's manner, so you start things carefully, with questions, with a plan. The opposition is a pull toward balance, and you'll feel it as a tug between your usual cool first impression and something warmer that keeps slipping out. You might hear yourself telling a near-stranger about your family. You might offer to help with something before you've been asked, and mean it. Earth and water get on well, so this doesn't have to feel like a struggle. It can feel like a relief, like being allowed to be kind in public.

In a new job it's becoming the person everyone brings their problems to, and being good at it. On a date it's the moment you stop assessing the other person and start enjoying them. With neighbours it's the spare key they hand you after a month. Who's been warming to you lately, and have you let them see the untidy side yet?
rising.reversed:
With the card reversed, Virgo rising can come across as the helper who won't be helped. You're efficient with new people, useful, a bit brisk, and nobody gets close enough to see what you might need. Pisces on your Descendant, turned upside down, can also mean attracting people who need rescuing, and taking on the job before you've even had a coffee with them.

At a new workplace you can end up with everyone's loose ends by the end of the month. In dating it's playing carer far too early. Socially it's being thought of as lovely and slightly unreachable. At the next first meeting, let the other person do something for you, even something as small as paying for the coffee.

sun.upright:
On paper this is the perfect card for a Libra Sun. Harmony, a happy couple, everyone in the right place. You want things to be fair and lovely and for everyone to get along, and you'd like to be known as the one who made that happen. It's close to what you're after. The catch is the planet. Mars is in detriment in Libra, working against the grain of your sign, which means the part of love that pushes, argues and fights for something is the part that comes least naturally to you.

That matters, because the happiness in this card has been through a few rows to get where it is. Pisces and Libra are quincunx as well, five signs apart and constantly adjusting, and water and air don't naturally mix, and don't clash either. You'll know it as the urge to keep the peace at a family dinner by smoothing over something that really needed saying. You get the nice evening. Then the same thing comes up again at the next dinner, a bit sharper, and you smooth it over again, and some part of you is keeping count.

With a partner this can be a relationship that's lovely on the surface and a little bit stuck. With in-laws or a blended family it's being the diplomat and quietly exhausted by it. At work it's the team that likes you and hasn't heard your real opinion. Pick one small thing you'd normally let slide at home and say it, kindly and clearly, and let the discomfort sit for a minute afterwards.
sun.reversed:
The peace-at-any-price habit gets expensive when this card is reversed. Mars in detriment in Libra sends the fight underground, and a Libra Sun can end up agreeing to a family arrangement that suits everyone except you, then resenting it with great charm. Or you put so much into looking like a happy couple that the actual couple gets neglected.

You'll find it in the holidays you didn't choose, the Sunday lunches you don't enjoy, and a partner who thinks everything's fine because you keep saying it is. Friends might get the charming version while the people at home get the tired one. Tell your partner one arrangement you'd like to change and suggest what you'd change it to. Don't soften it until it disappears.

moon.upright:
Raised voices go straight into a Libra Moon's body. You need peace to feel safe, and you'll do a lot to keep a room calm. This card is the room calm, the family together, the rainbow up, and it's a genuine comfort to draw it on this Moon. But look at the planet underneath. Mars is in detriment in Libra, so anger is the feeling you have the least practice with, and the elements, water and air, neither fight nor help each other.

What tends to happen is that you feel a flash of irritation and, before it's even landed, you've explained it away. They're tired, they didn't mean it, it's not worth it. The quincunx between Pisces and Libra adds a layer of constant small adjusting, and a Libra Moon can adjust so much it forgets which way it was originally facing. The happiness is real. It's also partly built on you swallowing things, and the card's gentleness can make that habit feel like a virtue.

In a partnership this looks like being the one who always apologises first. With friends it's being the go-between in someone else's falling out. In your body it's tension in the neck or the lower back, or a tiredness after family visits that doesn't make sense. The next time you feel annoyed, stay with it for a minute before you forgive. You can still forgive afterwards.
moon.reversed:
On a Libra Moon, the reversed card can mean keeping the peace until you can hardly breathe. You've swallowed so many small things for the sake of harmony at home that the harmony has started to feel like a performance. Mars in detriment here doesn't fight, it withdraws, so the anger shows up as coolness, a slightly too polite tone, a partner who asks what's wrong and gets 'nothing'.

Family gatherings bring it out, charming to everybody and flat on the drive home. In a relationship it's a gap opening up that neither of you names. Your body might answer with headaches or tight shoulders. Say one honest thing you've been sitting on to the person it concerns, and don't take it back when they look surprised.

rising.upright:
Most people decide within a minute that Libra rising is easy to like. You walk in pleasant and well put together, and the Ten of Cups adds a settled warmth to that, the look of someone who's content with their people. Strangers read you as partnered, or ready to be, even when you're not. Venus rules your Ascendant, and the card's picture of a couple who've made a home together fits the way you come across almost too neatly.

Mars is in detriment in Libra, though, and that's the part of the card that doesn't sit comfortably on you. You don't like to push at the start of anything. You wait, you read the room, you let other people set the tone, and in this card somebody has to actually build the home, and being pleasant in it isn't enough. The quincunx means small adjustments all the time. Air and water need an introduction. You may notice yourself going along with a group's plans for weeks before saying what you'd actually like to do.

In a new job it's being well liked and not quite taken seriously yet. In dating it's giving off 'partner material' so clearly that people fall a bit in love with the idea of you before they know you. With new friends it's agreeing to everything. Say one preference early in the next new friendship. Choose the restaurant.
rising.reversed:
Libra rising with this card upside down can look like the ideal partner and feel like nobody's home. You're agreeable with new people to the point of vanishing, and Mars in detriment keeps you from saying no, so you end up in arrangements you never chose. Or the harmony becomes a show, the perfect couple at the party with a row waiting in the car.

At work it's saying yes to a project because the person asking was nice. Socially it's too many invitations accepted and a calendar you dread. In a new relationship it's mirroring someone so well that they never meet you at all, and it usually takes them a few weeks to notice they've never heard you disagree. Decline one thing politely, without inventing a reason.

sun.upright:
Mars rules Scorpio, so the Ten of Cups is your own sign's ruler at work in Pisces, and that gives the card real weight for you. It speaks with the landlord's authority. Scorpio and Pisces are trine, both water, so the feeling in this card and the feeling in you are the same kind, deep and loyal, and the shared element turns the volume up. A Scorpio Sun wants to be known as the person who doesn't break, whose loyalty goes all the way down. This card is what that loyalty is for.

There's more to it. Mars also rules the first ten degrees of Scorpio, the decan of the Five of Cups, the figure in black staring at the spilled cups. So your sign holds both ends of this story, the loss and the fullness. A lot of Scorpio Suns I've met don't quite trust happiness. They've seen too much of the Five. When things are going well, part of you is watching for the catch, checking who might leave, keeping a little bit back. It feels like being realistic. It can also keep you at arm's length from the thing you've fought hardest to build.

In love, this card may be asking you to trust further than you usually would. With family, especially if you've lost someone, it can be a sense of the family putting itself back together. With money, it's the security you've built finally feeling like enough. Stop checking the locks, just for one evening. Stay in the room when things are good and let them be good.
sun.reversed:
This card reversed on a Scorpio Sun is loyalty turned possessive. Mars at home in your sign is strong in both directions, and upside down it guards the family so hard that nobody can breathe. Who's seeing whom, who said what at the barbecue, who might be pulling away. Or the Five of Cups side takes over and you brace so completely for loss that you pull away first.

With a partner you'll see it as jealousy that's hard to argue with, and with kids as a grip that tightens just as they need it loosened. At work it's treating the team as a family you have to defend against every outsider. Pick one person you've been watching closely and give them some room. Tell them you trust them, and then act as if you do.

moon.upright:
Water on water, and the card's planet is your Moon sign's own ruler. For a Scorpio Moon, that means the Ten of Cups lands with full force. You feel everything at depth and trust very few people with it, and you need loyalty, privacy and the truth. Pisces is trine to Scorpio, and Mars at home in your Moon's sign gives the card real authority here. The feelings are big. Love for your people, protectiveness, maybe a surge of gratitude you don't quite know what to do with.

Big water can be a lot to hold. Mars in Scorpio is fierce, and when it's this full of feeling it can tip into guarding. You love them so much you're afraid for them. The Five of Cups decan, the first stretch of Scorpio, is also Mars's, and for this Moon it often means happiness arrives with a memory of loss sitting quietly behind it. You'll notice it in the moments when everyone's laughing and you're suddenly thinking of the person who isn't there. That's grief doing what it does. It sits alongside the happiness without cancelling it.

With a partner it's intense closeness, and also watching carefully to see if it's safe. With family it's a loyalty that doesn't budge and a long memory for slights. In your body it's often held tension, a tight jaw, sleep that's deep and then suddenly not. Say out loud, to one person, how much they mean to you. Scorpio Moons tend to assume people know, and quite often they don't.
moon.reversed:
When this card reverses on a Scorpio Moon, the feeling goes under and stays there. Mars in its own sign doesn't let go, and the hurt from a family member or a partner gets stored, polished and kept for later. You go quiet. The people around you can feel the temperature drop and can't get you to say why. Sometimes it's grief that hasn't been let out, and it comes out as anger at the wrong person.

Sleep turns restless and full of dreams, and trust issues come out as checking. A sibling or parent might be at the centre of an old grudge. Tell the person what they did, in plain words, once. Then watch how they respond before you decide what it means about them.

rising.upright:
Even when it's trying not to, Scorpio rising gives off intensity. People feel sized up, and slightly fascinated. Mars is your traditional chart ruler, and the Ten of Cups puts it in Pisces, trine to your rising sign, water with water. It softens the look without weakening it. You come across as fiercely loyal, someone with a small circle they'd do anything for. Pisces is the fifth sign counting from Scorpio, so it sits on your fifth house, the house of romance, children and play, and the card's sign is sitting right where you have fun and fall in love.

That makes for an interesting first impression. The usual Scorpio guardedness is there, but there's warmth leaking round the edges, and people pick up on it. You may find strangers trusting you quickly, telling you things. Mars at home in your sign means the protectiveness is strong and unforced, and part of the tension is that you don't let people in easily, even when they're showing up keen. If your Ascendant falls in Scorpio's first ten degrees, Mars rules that slice as well, the Five of Cups decan, and you'll know how much you've lost before, and how that shapes who you let near.

On a first date it's the moment you let something personal slip and they lean in. At work it's being quietly adopted as the one who'd have someone's back. With kids, yours or anyone's, it's how gentle you turn out to be. Next time someone new is clearly warming to you, meet them halfway. Tell them something about your people.
rising.reversed:
Guarded to the point of cold is how Scorpio rising can come across with this reversed. The loyalty's there, but it's all pointed inward at your people, and newcomers feel like they're on the wrong side of a line. Mars as your chart ruler, strong and at home, makes that line hard to cross. Or you test people before you let them near, and some of the good ones fail because they didn't know they were sitting a test.

In a new job that means being respected and a bit feared. In dating it's the intensity that attracts people and then the wall they hit. At a family gathering with new partners around, it's the look you give them over the salad. Pick a new person and give them the benefit of the doubt on purpose, for a month.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius Suns want room. Room to travel, to think big, to believe in something and go after it. The Ten of Cups asks what all that roaming is coming home to, and for a lot of Sagittarians it's a slightly uncomfortable question. Pisces squares Sagittarius. They're both mutable and they sit at right angles to each other, which rubs until somebody moves. The two signs share a ruler, though, at least in the traditional scheme. Jupiter rules both, so there's a family resemblance under the friction, the same big-hearted generosity, one pointed at the horizon and one at the people close by.

Mars is a guest in your sign, coloured by Jupiter, so what the card puts behind you is enthusiasm, big plans for the family, the holiday, the house you'll buy one day. Fire and water don't agree, though. Inside, that can feel like being homesick and itchy at the same time. You miss your people when you're away, and a week at home with them makes you want to book a flight. That's the square at work, and it asks you to find a version of home that has some coming and going built into it.

With a partner it may be the conversation about settling down, or about how much freedom each of you needs inside it. With family far away it's the long-haul trip to see them. At work it's the job that would pay better and keep you on the road more. Plan something with your people that you'd genuinely look forward to, somewhere none of you has been, and book it.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, the card can show a Sagittarius Sun running from home and calling it freedom. The family plans get vague, the visits get shorter, and the big talk about the future stays talk. Or you idealise a far-off version of family, the life you'll have one day, the community somewhere else, and look past the people who are actually here.

Missed occasions give it away, the phone call you keep meaning to make, a partner who's tired of holding the fort. It can also come out as preaching about how families ought to work, which goes down badly over a family dinner. Ring the person you've been meaning to ring. Stay on for as long as they want to talk, even if it runs longer than you'd planned.

moon.upright:
Homesickness is an odd thing for a Sagittarius Moon to feel, and this card brings it, sometimes even when you're home. You need space to breathe and something to look forward to, and your feelings are usually big, quick and hopeful. The Ten of Cups adds a longing for your people and for a kind of belonging that's hard to pin down. Water and fire are opposed elements, and Pisces squares Sagittarius, so this doesn't sit quietly with you. It stirs things up.

Jupiter rules both signs in the old scheme, so the card and your Moon have the same generous planet behind them, and the longing tends to come out as openness. You want to throw the doors open and have everyone round, feed them, hear their news. Mars, a guest in Sagittarius and coloured by Jupiter, puts some push behind it. The tension is that you need to be able to leave as well. A Sagittarius Moon feels safest in a home with the door open, and the card's kind of belonging can feel, some days, like being asked to shut it.

With family this can be reconnecting with people you've drifted from, especially anyone far away. With a partner it's needing closeness and freedom in the same week, and feeling bad for asking for both. The body usually wants movement, a long walk, a swim, something outdoors. Go for the walk. Take someone you love with you, and let the conversation wander wherever it likes.
moon.reversed:
For a Sagittarius Moon, the reversed card turns restlessness into escape. Family closeness starts to feel smothering, so you plan the trip, pick up extra shifts, stay out late, anything to avoid the kitchen table. Or your beliefs about how family should be turn into a sermon, and the people you love feel lectured. Jupiter behind both signs makes all of it feel very justified.

A partner says you're never quite there. You turn up late to family events and leave early. Sleep might go restless, full of dreams about travel or about being somewhere you can't leave. Before you book anything, spend one evening at home doing nothing much with the people there. Notice when the urge to go kicks in, and what set it off.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising comes in open, friendly and a bit loud, and people like you on sight. With this card on your Ascendant there's something extra they pick up on, a warmth about home and family that doesn't usually lead the conversation. Pisces is the fourth sign from yours, so it sits on your fourth house, the base of the chart, where your roots are. The card's sign is right at your foundations, and some of that private ground is showing on the surface for once.

The square between Pisces and Sagittarius makes this lively. You're used to meeting people as the adventurer, the one with the stories, and here you might find yourself talking about your mum, or the house you grew up in, or wanting to settle somewhere. Mars is only a visitor on your Ascendant, coloured by Jupiter, which rules both Sagittarius and Pisces in the traditional scheme, so the push behind you is generous and a bit scattered. Fire and water are at odds. It can feel like two first impressions fighting over the same five minutes.

In a new workplace this looks like being the one who organises the social club and also the one who's always about to go travelling. On a date it's surprising the other person by how much you care about family. After a move, it's the neighbourhood you start treating like home within weeks. Mention your family early with someone new, and see who asks more about them.
rising.reversed:
Someone who won't commit is how Sagittarius rising can come across with the card reversed. New people sense the open road behind you and don't invest much. Or you overshare about family, the dramas, the estrangements, the funny uncle, in a way that feels like too much too soon. Mars as Jupiter's guest can make the first impression big and a bit careless.

At work it's the colleague who says they're only here for a year, three years in. In dating it's the talk of a future together on the second date, then the vanishing. Behind it, usually, is a question about where home is, and you haven't answered it yet. Slow down on the big statements. Say one small true thing about where you come from and leave it there.

sun.upright:
Mars is exalted in Capricorn, an honoured guest, the planet at its most disciplined, so with a Capricorn Sun the card's drive has never been in better hands. You want to build something that lasts and be respected for having built it. What this card shows is a finished family, a home that holds, and that's the sort of long project a Capricorn understands. Pisces and Capricorn are sextile, an easy opening you still have to use, and water and earth get on well. Things grow slowly and stay.

The tension is in where the effort goes. Your version of love is often provision. You work hard so they'll be secure, you're proud of that, and you should be. Look at the people in the card, though. Nobody's working. Everyone in it has stopped. From the inside you'll know how hard it is to switch off at home, to leave the email alone, to be in the room without a job to do. Mars also rules the middle ten degrees of Capricorn, the decan of the Three of Pentacles, which is the card of skilled work done alongside other people. That's your comfort zone. Home life that isn't a project is the part you're less sure of.

In your career it may be that the work you've put in has finally made the family secure. With a partner there's the holiday you keep saying you'll take when things calm down. With your parents it's finally being seen by them as having made it. Book the holiday. Tell your partner the dates before you tell work.
sun.reversed:
This reversed on a Capricorn Sun can mean the work has swallowed the home. You're providing so well that you're never there, and the family has learned to get on without you. Mars, exalted in your sign, is very good at pushing on, and upside down it pushes on past the point where anybody at home is still waiting up. Or you're running the household like a business, schedules, targets, expectations, and wondering why nobody's having fun.

A partner stops asking when you'll be home. Kids or younger relatives come to you for money and to someone else for comfort. Your parents' idea of success may be driving more of this than you'd like to admit. Leave work at a set time one evening, without warning anyone, and turn up for dinner.

moon.upright:
Bills paid, plans made, nobody relying on luck. That's what a Capricorn Moon needs before it can relax. It tends to show love through responsibility, and it doesn't cry easily in front of people. What this card brings is a softer kind of security, the kind that comes from being loved, which you don't have to earn. Pisces is sextile to Capricorn and water and earth are friends, so it's a welcome visitor. Mars is exalted in Capricorn, the planet at its most dignified, which means even your anger tends to be controlled and put to work.

You'll probably notice how hard it is to simply receive. Someone makes you dinner and you start clearing up before you've finished eating. Someone says they're proud of you and you change the subject. The card's warmth is asking you to let the guard down a little, and an exalted Mars in your Moon's sign is very good at keeping it up. Feelings get managed. Often that works fine. Sometimes the family can't tell you're sad until you're very sad.

With your parents, especially whoever was the authority figure, there might be a moment of real warmth or recognition. With a partner it's being the rock and occasionally wishing someone would let you be the one who falls apart. Your body tends to hold it in the shoulders and the back. Let someone look after you in some small, practical way. Don't pay them back straight away.
moon.reversed:
When this reverses on a Capricorn Moon, feelings go into lockdown. You cope. You cope so well that nobody, including you, notices how lonely it's got. Mars exalted in your Moon's sign can turn control into coldness, and the family starts treating you as the manager of the house instead of one of the people in it. Some Capricorn Moons go the other way and feel every family obligation as a weight, dutiful and joyless.

It sits in a tight jaw, in sleep that doesn't quite rest you, and in a partner who's stopped bringing you their problems because you go straight to solutions. A parent might be pressing on an old nerve. Say out loud, to someone you trust, one thing you're finding hard. Leave the solution out of it.

rising.upright:
People hand Capricorn rising the clipboard. You come across as serious, capable and a bit older than your years, the one they'd want in charge in an emergency. The Ten of Cups gives that authority a warmer face. People see you as someone who's built something solid for the people you love, and that makes them trust you. Mars is exalted in Capricorn, so the card's planet is honoured on your Ascendant, strong and well used. Pisces is your third sign along, the third house of siblings, neighbours and everyday talk, and that's often where the card's warmth shows up first.

Your usual first impression is reserved, and people take a while to get past it. This card shortens that. You might catch yourself chatting with the neighbour over the fence, or getting properly close to a sibling again, or being unexpectedly warm with a new colleague. Pisces and Capricorn are sextile, which is an easy opening, but you do have to use it. If your Ascendant sits in the middle of Capricorn, ten to nineteen degrees, Mars rules that stretch as well, the Three of Pentacles decan, and a lot of this will happen through shared work, a project, a build, a team.

At work it's being the calm manager everyone likes working for. With neighbours it's the street barbecue you end up organising. With a brother or sister it's picking up the phone more than you have in years. Knock on a neighbour's door with a reason, any reason. Borrow something.
rising.reversed:
The reversed card can make Capricorn rising look like it has no time for anyone. You come across as busy, self-sufficient and a little severe, and people assume your life is sorted and don't offer. Mars exalted on your Ascendant pushes hard and competently, and reversed, the competence turns into a wall. Or the family image is so polished, the achievements, the tidy house, that new people feel slightly judged in your company.

At work it's being respected and left off the invitations. With neighbours it's a nod and nothing more for years. Siblings may feel it too. In a new relationship it's showing the CV version of yourself on the first three dates. Let someone see you not coping with something small. Ask a neighbour for help with it.

sun.upright:
Chosen family is a very Aquarian idea, and the Ten of Cups doesn't mind what shape a family takes, which suits you. An Aquarius Sun wants to be fully itself and to belong to something bigger, a group, a cause, a way of thinking. This card is belonging too, but a closer, warmer kind, and for a lot of Aquarians that's the harder one. Pisces comes straight after Aquarius, and signs that sit side by side like that have little in common, each with what the other lacks. Aquarius thinks about everybody. Pisces feels for everybody. Water and air have to be introduced before they'll work together.

Mars holds no rank in Aquarius and takes its tone from Saturn in the old scheme and Uranus in the modern one, so the card's drive comes through as principle, doing right by your people, sticking to your own way of doing family. It can feel like being loyal and a bit detached at once. You'd do anything for the family. You'd also like them to stop asking how you feel about it. The friends who've become family count just as much to you as anyone related by blood, and this card agrees.

With friends this is often the group becoming something closer, the shared house, the regular dinners, the people who show up. With your family of origin it might be finding a way to be yourself around them that doesn't need a fight. With a partner it's letting them see how much you care. Tell one person in your chosen family what they mean to you, in words, even if it feels awkward to say.
sun.reversed:
For an Aquarius Sun, the reversed card can mean keeping your family at a principled distance. You love them in theory. In practice you're busy, you're elsewhere, you're doing things your own way, and they've stopped expecting you. Mars coloured by Saturn makes it dutiful when it isn't distant, the birthday card sent on time and nothing else. Or you've built a chosen family and hold it to ideals nobody can live up to.

Family events you skip on principle are the giveaway, and friends who feel a bit managed. A partner might be wanting you closer and not know how to ask. Pick one family obligation you'd normally skip and turn up. Stay for the whole thing, and be curious about the people there.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon needs a bit of distance from its own feelings to feel safe. You like to understand an emotion before you let it in. This card brings something warmer and closer than you might be used to, and the elements, air and water, don't take to each other on their own. You may find yourself unexpectedly moved, at a wedding, by an old photo, by a friend who's always there, and a bit unsure what to do with it.

Pisces and Aquarius sit side by side in the zodiac and have little in common. The card has the closeness you hold back from, and you have the clear head it could use. Mars is a guest in Aquarius, coloured by Saturn and Uranus, and it makes strong feelings come out a bit sideways, as a debate, a principle, a sudden need to be alone. You'll notice you feel closest to people in groups, and a bit panicky one on one, when someone looks at you and asks how you really are.

With friends this can be the group chat that turns into real support. With a partner it's letting them see you moved without explaining it away. With family it's feeling close to them from a distance and awkward in the same room. Usually it's the friend who turns up uninvited with soup who gets through to you.
moon.reversed:
This card reversed on an Aquarius Moon can mean detachment turning into distance. You're fine, you say, and you mean it, and meanwhile you haven't let anyone close in months. Mars coloured by Saturn gets dutiful about feelings, doing the right thing by the family without feeling much while you do it. Uranus, the modern ruler of your Moon's sign, can make you pull away abruptly when someone gets close.

A partner starts to feel they're living with a flatmate, and friends only ever see the fun side of you. Groups are easy. The one-on-one is where you go missing. Let one person in on something that's actually bothering you, even if you have to write it down first and hand it to them.

rising.upright:
Friendly, a little unusual, easy to talk to and hard to know. That's how most people read Aquarius rising. The Ten of Cups on your Ascendant gives it a warmer face. People see someone with a real community, a group that's become family, and they're drawn in. Pisces is the next sign along from Aquarius, which puts it on your second house, the house of money and what you value, and belonging is likely to feel like a kind of wealth to you. People pick that up.

Pisces and Aquarius are neighbours with little in common, and the elements are neutral to each other, so nothing flows automatically. The warmth sits a bit oddly on your cool front. You might find you're more open with new people than usual and then wonder if you overdid it. Mars, a guest in Aquarius, coloured by Saturn and Uranus, starts things in its own particular way, and your way of welcoming people will be a bit unconventional too, the potluck, the group walk, the club you start yourself.

At work this is being the one who brings people together across teams. In friendship it's a new group adopting you, or you adopting them. In dating it's coming across as someone who wants a real partnership, which may surprise people who had you down as a free spirit. Start something small that gets people in a room together. A monthly dinner is plenty.
rising.reversed:
Holding everyone at arm's length is the risk for Aquarius rising with the card reversed. You're friendly with all and close to none, and new people sense they won't get past the first layer. Mars in Aquarius, coloured by Saturn, makes the first impression cool and a little formal. Or you project an ideal community, the perfect group, the right values, and people feel they have to pass a test to join.

At work it's being liked and never trusted with anything personal. In a new friendship group it's being there for the causes and missing at the birthdays. Neighbours know your name and nothing else about you. Show up at one small, ordinary, personal thing, a birthday, a house-warming, and stay long enough to have a real conversation.

sun.upright:
Draw this for a Pisces Sun and you've pulled one of your own sign's cards. The Ten of Cups is one of Pisces's three decan cards, the one for its final stretch, twenty to twenty-nine degrees. If your Sun is late in Pisces, this is literally your card. Even if it isn't, the card speaks your sign's language, water in water, and it shows what a Pisces Sun is quietly hoping to build, a life where love is the point and everyone's included.

Mars has no dignity in Pisces. It's a visitor, and it takes its colour from Jupiter, the traditional ruler, and Neptune, the modern one. Jupiter makes the drive generous. Neptune makes it idealistic. You'll recognise that you'd fight for a dream of family harder than for almost anything else, and that the dream can sometimes get ahead of the real people in it. This is the end of the zodiac, the last part of the last sign, and there's a completeness about the card you might feel as a kind of peace. There's also the risk of expecting the peace to turn up by itself.

With a partner this may be a period of real closeness, the sense of having found your person. With family it's the urge to heal old rifts and bring everyone together. In creative work it might be a project about home and belonging and where you come from. Pick one real, practical step toward the family life you picture. Make the phone call, or set the date.
sun.reversed:
A Pisces Sun with this card reversed can lose itself in the family. Mars, a visitor in your sign, goes soft and scattered, and all your drive gets spent on keeping everybody else happy. Your own plans dissolve. Or the Neptune side wins and you're living in the dream of how family ought to be, disappointed over and over by the people who are actually there.

Sacrifices nobody asked for pile up, along with a quiet resentment you'd never admit to. A partner might feel idealised and never quite known. Work drifts while you look after everyone. Choose one thing that's only yours, a class, an evening, a project, and protect it the way you'd protect someone you love.

moon.upright:
Every room you walk into, a Pisces Moon picks up the mood, and a lot of what you feel isn't even yours. Here it's water in water, the card's own sign sitting right on your emotional home, and the effect is to fill you right up. Moments of real happiness with the people you love can bring you close to tears. So can other people's happiness, or a film, or a song on the radio.

With that much water it's easy to lose the edges. Mars is a guest in Pisces with no dignity, taking its colour from Jupiter and Neptune, and in the Moon's sign it tends to mean anger doesn't know how to come out. It dissolves. It turns into sadness, or tiredness, or a need to be alone that you can't quite explain. The card's warmth is real, and it can also make you so keen to keep the peace that you let go of things that needed saying. You'll forgive before anyone's even apologised.

With a partner this can be deep closeness and the risk of losing yourself in them. With family it's being the emotional sponge at gatherings and needing a lie-down afterwards. Sleep is where a lot of this gets processed, vivid dreams, a need to sleep longer. Give yourself time alone after big family occasions, and don't apologise for taking it.
moon.reversed:
When this card is upside down on a Pisces Moon, the feelings flood and there's nowhere firm to stand. You take on everyone's moods at home, and your own get lost underneath. Mars has no special standing in Pisces and takes on the sign's softness, so it won't push for what you need, and you drift, or withdraw, or escape, a lot of screens, a lot of sleep, a glass of wine that turns into two.

Exhaustion that rest doesn't fix is one sign. A partner who can't tell what you want because you've stopped saying is another. The dream of a close, perfect family can also become a place to hide from the one you've got. Say one clear no to somebody at home. Then notice that they're still fine, and so are you.

rising.upright:
Strangers tell Pisces rising things. You meet the world softly, gentle, a bit dreamy, easy to talk to and hard to pin down. This is one of your rising sign's own decan cards, covering the end of Pisces from twenty degrees on, so drawn for your mask it looks very natural on you. Water in water. What people meet is someone who seems to belong, and who makes them feel like they could belong too. They invite you home.

Mars is a visitor in Pisces, coloured by Jupiter and Neptune, and it isn't a pushy one. Your way of starting things is to drift into them, to be invited, to be carried along. The card adds warmth and a sense of family around you, and the challenge is that it's so easy to become whatever the other person needs. You meet a new group and within an hour you're the one who understands everyone. That's lovely. It can also mean nobody's quite sure what you want.

In a new job this looks like becoming the heart of the team almost by accident. In dating it's being so tuned in that the other person feels they've known you for years. With a new friend it's being asked to Sunday lunch with their family after one coffee. Go. And while you're there, tell them one clear preference, even about something small, like how you take your tea.
rising.reversed:
Like a mirror, Pisces rising with this card reversed shows people what they want to see. You go along with it, and nobody meets you. Mars, only a visitor in Pisces, makes it hard to set a boundary at the start, so you end up agreeing to things out of kindness and slipping away from them later, usually by text. Neptune, the modern ruler of your sign, makes the blur worse.

At work it's being everyone's confidant and nobody's first choice for the promotion. In dating it's becoming whoever the other person wants and then feeling lost. At a family gathering with new people it's soaking up all the tension in the room, and needing a whole day to recover afterwards. Pick one first meeting and bring a firm opinion to it, about anything at all.

1.upright:
Your body, your face, the way you walk into a room and the way you start things, that's the first house. Mars is its natural ruler, so with the Ten of Cups here the card is on home turf. What's live is how much your people have become part of how you present. You may notice you're walking a bit taller because someone's proud of you, or that you've started introducing yourself as somebody's partner, somebody's mum, somebody's mate, before you get round to your job.

The friction is elemental. The first house's natural sign is Aries, fire, and the card is water, from Pisces, the sign just behind Aries. Those two elements are opposed, and you'll feel it as a pull between acting for yourself and acting for everyone. You start something for you, a new haircut, a new routine, a fresh plan, and it keeps turning into something for the family. The first house is angular, one of the four corners of the chart, so other people see this change in you quite clearly, even if you haven't mentioned it.

In your body it might show as more energy when home life is good, and noticeably less when it isn't. In how you begin things it's projects started with other people in mind, the course that would help the household, the job that fits around school hours. Let one new start be purely for you. It can be small, as long as it's yours.
1.reversed:
The body picks up family strain quickly when this card sits upside down in the first house. Mars, the house's own ruler, gets pulled in every direction, and the energy that should go into you goes into holding everyone else up. You might look fine and feel flat. Or you're so identified with the role, parent, carer, partner, that you've lost track of what you'd do if nobody needed you. Fire and water pull against each other here, and water is winning.

You'll see it in the mirror, the tired face, the clothes chosen for practicality, and in how often you start sentences with 'we'. The hobby you quietly dropped says the same thing. Give your body something that's only for it, a swim, a walk alone, an early night, and don't give it away when someone asks.

2.upright:
Actual money and actual self-worth, what's in the account and what you think you're worth, that's second-house territory. With the Ten of Cups here, family sits at the centre of both. Money is likely to be about the household, the joint budget, saving for the home, paying for the things that make everyone's life easier. Self-worth gets tied up with providing, with being able to give your people what they need, and feeling good about yourself when you can.

The tension is Mars.
